header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue #145: "Add descriptions to categories" in this repo (expense-tracker).

## Goal
Add an optional free-text `description` to a category that states what kind of expense belongs in it. It must be settable/editable/clearable in the UI, carried through the API, fed into the AI category-selection prompt, and exposed over MCP.

## Acceptance criteria (must all hold)
- A user can set, edit and clear a category description, with the length limit enforced and a clear validation error shown.
- Existing categories keep working with no description (the column is nullable; a blank description is stored as absent/NULL).
- The AI category-selection prompt includes each category's description when present; covered by a test using the fake Bedrock client (no external calls).
- `list_categories` (MCP) exposes the description.
- All category queries stay scoped by `user_id`.

## Scope and design decisions (already decided, follow exactly)

### Data + API
- New nullable `description` column on the `category` table via a new evolution file `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/17.sql` (highest existing is 16.sql). App-level validation only: no DB CHECK constraint and no column DEFAULT for the business rule.
- Limit: description trimmed, max 500 characters; blank -> stored as absent (NULL).
- Thread `description` through the Tapir request/response models in `lib/api/shared` (these already exist: `CreateCategory`, `UpdateCategory`, `GetCategories` under `.../api/models/categories/`). Endpoint definitions stay in `lib/api/shared`, never in `server/`.
- Update `CategoryDAO` (`server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/CategoryDAO.scala`) and the corresponding action(s): parser, INSERT, UPDATE, SELECT. Keep every query user-scoped (`WHERE user_id = ?`) and every list query with a stable `ORDER BY`.
- Use Chimney `transformInto` for case-class shape mapping where applicable, matching existing style.

### Validated field (important)
- Introduce a validated primitive `CategoryDescription` in `lib/common/shared` with a `TextValidator`, mirroring how existing primitives like `Name`/`Email`/`Password` are defined and validated. The 500-char/trim/blank-is-absent rule lives in that validator and is shared by the API and the web form (no duplicate ad-hoc checks). If a `CategoryName` validated primitive does not already exist, prefer reusing whatever the category name currently uses rather than inventing a parallel one; do not change the existing name semantics.

### Web form (important)
- Convert ONLY the category create + edit form on `CategoriesPage` (`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/CategoriesPage.scala`) to the template's typed-form pattern: a `FormData[Request]` built from `FormField[T: TextValidator]`, driven by `StatefulFormData`. Use the existing library types from package `net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.forms` (`FormData`, `FormField`, `StatefulFormData`). The canonical in-repo templates to copy are `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/UpdateInfoFormData.scala` together with `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/widgets/EditUserForm.scala` (and `SignInForm.scala`). Create a new `CategoryFormData` in `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/` holding the name and description fields and producing the create/update request via `submitRequest`.
- Do NOT touch the other places categories get created on the fly (the free-solo autocomplete category creation in the expense/refund/import-rule forms, and the create-category modal on `MerchantsPage`). Those are autocomplete flows that do not fit `FormField`. For those, only make sure the new `description` field flows through the shared API models; do not refactor them to `FormData`.
- Show the description as helper text where a category is picked, only where it fits without clutter.
- Frontend reachability: the create/edit form is already reachable on `CategoriesPage`; no new route is needed. Confirm the edited form still renders and is reachable.

### AI
- When a category has a description, include it in the category-selection prompt built in `StatementSuggestionsService`. If the JEV variant (`JevStatementSuggestionsService`) also selects categories by name, include it there too. Add/extend a test using the existing fake Bedrock client to assert the description appears in the prompt when present. No external API calls in tests.

### MCP
- `list_categories` must return the description. Update `McpTools`/`McpDispatcher` and the MCP tests accordingly.

## Tests
- Add/update server tests (testcontainers Postgres + fakes) for: DAO/action round-trip of description, validation rejecting an over-limit description with a clear error, blank-stored-as-absent, the AI prompt including descriptions (fake Bedrock), and MCP `list_categories` exposing it.
- Add/update a web test for the converted `CategoriesPage` form if the existing test conventions cover it (see `docs/guide/testing.md`); component tests use `BrowserRouter` + jsdom.

## Hard constraints (repo is PUBLIC)
- The PR title, body and all commit messages must contain NO PII: no real bank names, account numbers/last4, real filenames, merchant names, or amounts. Use placeholders.
- Do NOT put any claude.ai session link in commits or the PR. `Co-Authored-By` lines are fine.
- Custom wart `NamedArguments`: when a call has 2+ arguments of the same type they MUST be passed by name or it fails to compile.
- No silent defaults for missing data: validation fails loudly with a clear error; never fabricate a value.

## If the code differs from this spec
If something in the codebase does not match what is described above (different field names, an existing validated primitive, a different suggestions-prompt structure, etc.), adapt to the actual code rather than forcing the spec, keep the acceptance criteria intact, and document each such deviation in a short "Spec deviations" section of the PR description.

resultJson.description:
Add an optional free-text `description` to categories (GitHub issue #145). It says what kind of expense belongs in the category. The user can set, edit and clear it on CategoriesPage. It is stored in a new nullable `category.description` column and returned by the categories API. It is also fed to the AI category-selection prompts (Bedrock `StatementSuggestionsService` and the JEV variant `JevStatementSuggestionsService`) so the model can pick categories more accurately, and it is returned by the MCP `list_categories` tool. Existing categories keep working with no description: the column is nullable and a blank description is stored as NULL.

The business rule (trim, at most 500 characters, blank means absent) lives in one place: a new validated primitive `CategoryDescription` in `lib/common/shared`. The server actions (through a validator in `server/.../validations/`) and the web form both use it. The server fails loudly with the exact message "Description must be 500 characters or less"; it never truncates or fabricates a value. The category create/edit UI on CategoriesPage moves to the template's typed-form pattern (`FormData`/`FormField`/`StatefulFormData`) via a new `CategoryFormData`. The other on-the-fly category creation flows (free-solo autocompletes, the MerchantsPage modal, Telegram) are not refactored; they only keep compiling and send no description.

Known spec deviations, already decided (record them in the PR's "Spec deviations" section): (1) No category-name validated primitive exists. Name validation today is an inline check (non-blank, at most 25 chars, messages "The name is required" / "Name must be 25 characters or less"), and `Name` (min length 2) would change those semantics. So we add a `CategoryName` primitive that mirrors the current rule and messages exactly, because `FormField` requires a `TextValidator`. (2) The API models keep `name: String` and `description: Option[String]`, not the wrapped types. Validation runs in the action through the shared validator, so the client gets a clear error message instead of an opaque JSON decode failure. (3) `CreateCategory` keeps its get-or-create semantics. When the name already exists (including a case-variant), the existing category is returned and its description is left unchanged. (4) The JEV variant also selects categories, so it gets the description in its criteria text too.

tasks.title: Add CategoryName and CategoryDescription validated primitives in lib/common
tasks.description:
Create `lib/common/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/common/models/CategoryName.scala` and `CategoryDescription.scala`, both `class X private (val string: String) extends WrappedString` with `object X extends WrappedString.Companion[X]`, mirroring `Name.scala`.

CategoryName.validate(s) must mirror today's server rule exactly, with no trimming of the stored value: if `s.isBlank` → Invalid("The name is required"); else if `s.length > 25` → Invalid("Name must be 25 characters or less"); else Valid(s, new CategoryName(s)). Expose `val MaxLength = 25`.

CategoryDescription: `val MaxLength = 500`. validate(s) trims; if the trimmed length > 500 → Invalid(input = s, error = "Description must be 500 characters or less"); else Valid(s, new CategoryDescription(trimmed)). An empty or blank input is Valid with an empty value. Add `def parseOptional(raw: Option[String]): Either[String, Option[CategoryDescription]]`: None, or blank after trim → Right(None); invalid → Left(error message); otherwise Right(Some(trimmed value)). Both the server and the web use this to apply blank-is-absent.

Add `CategoryNameSpec` and `CategoryDescriptionSpec` under `lib/common/shared/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/common/models/`, following `NameSpec`. Cover: boundary 25/26 for the name and its blank error; for the description, exactly 500 (valid), 501 (invalid, exact message), surrounding whitespace trimmed (so 500 chars plus spaces is valid), and parseOptional for None, "   ", a valid value, and an over-limit value.

Verify: `CI=true sbt "commonJVM/testOnly *CategoryNameSpec *CategoryDescriptionSpec"` (check build.sbt for the exact project id) and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Persist category description: evolution 17, model, DAO, repository
tasks.description:
Add `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/17.sql` in the same style as 16.sql (`-- !Ups` plus a comment): `ALTER TABLE category ADD COLUMN description TEXT NULL;`. Add no CHECK constraint and no DEFAULT.

Add `description: Option[String]` right after `name` in `repositories/models/Category.scala`, in both `Category` and `Category.Create`. Update `categoryParser` in `repositories/daos/package.scala` (Macro.parser column list: add "description" after "name").

In `CategoryDAO`, add the `description` column to `create`, `createIfAbsent`, and the SELECT lists of `all`/`find`/`findByName`. Change `update` to `update(id, userId, name, description: Option[String], updatedAt)` and SET both name and description. Keep every WHERE `user_id = ?` and keep `ORDER BY name` in `all`. Pass all same-typed args by name (NamedArguments wart).

In `CategoriesRepository`: change `getOrCreate(userId, name, description: Option[String])`; on conflict it returns the existing row unchanged. Change `update(id, userId, name, description: Option[String])`.

Update all compile-time callers. Telegram callers (`TelegramExpenseService` x2, `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction`) pass `description = None`. `CreateCategoryAction`/`UpdateCategoryAction` temporarily pass `None` (wired properly in the next task). Fix the positional test helpers `Category(UUID.randomUUID(), userId, name, now, now)` in `StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec` and `JevStatementSuggestionsServiceSpec` (add `None`). Add an optional `description: Option[String] = None` param to `RepositoryUtils.createCategory`.

Tests in `CategoriesRepositorySpec`: a create with a description round-trips through `find` and `all`; a create without one reads back None; `update` sets, changes and clears (None) the description; `update` by another user still fails with "Category not found"; `getOrCreate` with a description on an existing name leaves the stored description unchanged.

Verify: `CI=true sbt "server/testOnly *CategoriesRepositorySpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Thread description through the categories API with shared validation
tasks.description:
In `lib/api/shared/.../api/models/categories/`:
- `CreateCategory.Request(name: String, description: Option[String] = None)`
- `UpdateCategory.Request(name: String, description: Option[String])`. This is a full replacement, so None clears the description. No default, so callers must decide.
- `GetCategories.Response.Category(id, name, description: Option[String] = None, createdAt)`. Put the default where it keeps existing named call sites compiling, and fix positional call sites in web tests and main (`MerchantsPage`, `CategoryResolver`, web specs) as needed. Leave `CreateCategory.Response` unchanged.

`Json.format` treats Option as nullable, so an absent key reads as None. Endpoints stay in `lib/api/shared/.../endpoints/CategoriesEndpoints.scala`; no change is expected there.

Add a validator `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/validations/ValidateCategoryFields.scala`, e.g. `object ValidateCategoryFields { def apply(name: String, description: Option[String]): Future[Option[CategoryDescription]] }`. It uses `CategoryName.validate` (same messages as today) and `CategoryDescription.parseOptional`, and fails with `RuntimeException(<validator message>)`. Replace the inline `validateFormat`/`validate` in `CreateCategoryAction` and `UpdateCategoryAction` with this validator (RULE-BE-009). The actions then pass `description.map(_.string)` to `categoriesRepository.getOrCreate` / `update`. `GetCategoriesAction` already uses Chimney `transformInto`, so description maps automatically; confirm it compiles.

In `web/.../CategoriesPage.scala`, the existing rename call must preserve the description until the form conversion task: `UpdateCategory.Request(name = renameValue, description = cat.description)`. Free-solo/autocomplete creators (`BulkExpenseCreationPage`, `CategoryResolver`, `BankRowCreateRefundForm`, `MerchantsPage`) are not refactored; they keep sending no description.

Tests in `server/src/test/scala/controllers/CategoriesControllerSpec.scala`: create with a description → `getCategories` returns it; create with "   " → stored as None; create with 501 chars → error "Description must be 500 characters or less"; 500 chars plus surrounding spaces → accepted and trimmed; update sets, edits and clears (None and blank) the description; update with an over-limit description fails with the same message; existing name-validation tests keep their exact messages. Other users can't see the description (existing isolation test pattern).

Verify: `CI=true sbt "server/testOnly *CategoriesControllerSpec *CategoriesRepositorySpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Include category descriptions in the AI category-selection prompts
tasks.description:
In `server/.../services/StatementSuggestionsService.scala` `categoryPrompt`: when `c.description` is non-empty, add an indented line under the category's `- <name>` line, e.g. `    description: ${oneLine(d)}`, before the example lines. Adjust the header sentence so it mentions the optional description, e.g. "Categories, each with an optional description of what belongs in it and descriptions of transactions the user previously filed under it:". Keep `<category name>` in the answer instructions, because the test fake classifies prompts by that string. Categories without a description render exactly as today.

In `JevStatementSuggestionsService.predictCategory`, the criteria value is currently `name` or `name. Examples: ...`. Insert the description when present, e.g. `${oneLine(c.name)}: ${oneLine(d)}` followed by the existing `. Examples: ...` suffix. Keys stay category ids.

Tests, using only the in-spec fakes with no external calls:
- `StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec`: build a category with `description = Some("Supermarket food shopping")` and one without. Assert the category prompt includes the description text and that the other category's line has no `description:` line.
- `JevStatementSuggestionsServiceSpec`: assert the criteria for the described category contain the description. Update the existing exact-criteria expectation in the "key category criteria by id, describe them with examples" test only if its categories gain a description; otherwise leave it as-is to prove there is no change when absent.

Verify: `CI=true sbt "server/testOnly *StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec *JevStatementSuggestionsServiceSpec"`.

tasks.title: Expose category description via MCP list_categories
tasks.description:
`McpDispatcher` already serializes `GetCategoriesAction`'s `GetCategories.Response` with `Json.toJson`, so `description` flows automatically. play-json omits None keys. Update the `list_categories` tool description text in `server/.../mcp/McpTools.scala` to say each category may include an optional `description` of what kind of expense belongs in it. Optionally mention it in the McpDispatcher `instructions` string only if that reads naturally.

Tests: in `server/src/test/scala/controllers/McpControllerSpec.scala`, extend or add a `list_categories` case that creates one category with a description and one without through `client.createCategory(CreateCategory.Request(name = ..., description = Some(...)))`. Assert the description is present for the first and absent (or null) for the second, and that only the authenticated user's categories are returned. If `McpDispatcherSpec` asserts tool metadata text, update it accordingly.

Verify: `CI=true sbt "server/testOnly *McpControllerSpec *McpDispatcherSpec"`.

tasks.title: Convert CategoriesPage create/edit to typed CategoryFormData with description
tasks.description:
Create `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/CategoryFormData.scala`, modelled on `UpdateInfoFormData`: `case class CategoryFormData(name: FormField[CategoryName], description: FormField[CategoryDescription]) extends FormData[CreateCategory.Request]`.
- `fields = List(name, description)`; `formValidationErrors = List(fieldsError).flatten`.
- `submitRequest`: the name comes from `name.valueOpt`. The description is None when the field is untouched (`value == None`) or blank; Some(trimmed) when valid; and the whole request is None when the description is Invalid. Reuse `CategoryDescription.parseOptional` on the field's raw input rather than duplicating checks.
- Add `def updateRequest: Option[UpdateCategory.Request]`, built from `submitRequest` by copying name and description by name (Chimney is not on the web classpath).
- `object CategoryFormData { def initial(nameLabel: String, descriptionLabel: String, name: Option[CategoryName] = None, description: Option[CategoryDescription] = None): CategoryFormData }`. The name field is `required = true`; the description field is not required.
- Before relying on how `fieldsError`, `valueOpt` and `required` behave for an optional untouched field, read the library source: `net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.forms.{FormData, FormField, StatefulFormData}` from `slinky-utils_sjs1_3-0.7.2.jar` in `~/.cache/coursier/v1/https/repo1.maven.org/maven2/net/wiringbits/slinky-utils_sjs1_3/0.7.2/`, or from GitHub wiringbits/wiringbits-webapp-utils under `slinky-utils/src/main/scala/.../forms/`.

Add inputs to `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/components/inputs/inputs.scala`: `object CategoryNameInput extends ValidatedTextInput[CategoryName]` and `object CategoryDescriptionInput extends ValidatedTextInput[CategoryDescription]`.

Rewrite the create form and the per-category edit (currently "Rename") in `web/.../components/pages/CategoriesPage.scala` (`CategoryList`). Copy the `EditUserForm` submit structure exactly (AP-FE-06): `Hooks.useState(StatefulFormData(CategoryFormData.initial(...)))`, `onDataChanged` via `current.filling.copy(data = f(current.data))`, `isSubmitButtonEnabled` → `setFormData(_.submit)` → `submitRequest.orElse { submissionFailed(...); None }` → API call → `submitted` or `submissionFailed(ex.getMessage)`, and show `formData.firstValidationError` / the server error with an error label.
- Create: name + description → `createCategory`. On success, reset to `initial` and refresh.
- Edit: rename the button to "Edit". Opening it initialises a separate edit `StatefulFormData` with `CategoryName.trusted(cat.name)` and `cat.description.map(CategoryDescription.trusted)`. Save calls `updateCategory(cat.id, updateRequest)`, so clearing the description field sends None.
- In the list card, show `cat.description` under the name as secondary text when present.

Keep search and pagination as they are. Don't use object-level vals for elements (AP-FE-01/02), and add no new `js.Dynamic`/`asInstanceOf` in the page (AP-FE-07). Labels are hardcoded English, as in the current page.

Tests: `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/CategoryFormDataSpec.scala`, following `UpdateInfoFormDataSpec`. Cover: valid name only → request with description None; name + blank description → None; name + valid description → trimmed Some; over-limit description → `formValidationErrors` non-empty and `submitRequest` None; invalid (blank) name → None; `updateRequest` mirrors `submitRequest`; `fields` names.

Only add a jsdom render-without-crash test for `CategoryList` if you can justify it under RULE-TE-010 (a guard against element reuse in the new form tree); use BrowserRouter + jsdom with `null.asInstanceOf[API]`, documented, since render doesn't call the API. The page is already reachable at its existing route in `AppRouter.scala` and from navigation, so no routing change is needed; confirm it still compiles and renders.

Verify: `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *CategoryFormDataSpec"` (Node 24 must be on PATH) and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Show the selected category's description as helper text in the bank-row expense form
tasks.description:
Add a pure helper to `web/.../components/pages/AutocompleteLabels.scala`: `private[pages] def categoryDescription(categories: List[GetCategories.Response.Category], selectedId: Option[UUID]): Option[String]`. It returns the selected category's non-blank description.

In `bankstatementreview/BankRowCreateExpenseForm.scala`, render that description as small secondary text (theme token or CSS var color, no hex) directly under the category autocomplete when a category is selected and has a description. This is the main pick-a-category flow. Do not change its free-solo create logic or convert it to FormData. Do not add the helper to other pickers unless it fits just as cleanly; leave the multi-split and bulk pages alone to avoid clutter.

Tests: extend `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/AutocompleteLabelsSpec.scala` with cases for the helper: selected with a description, selected without, nothing selected, unknown id. No DOM test.

Verify: `CI=true sbt "web/testOnly *AutocompleteLabelsSpec *BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- lib/common/shared (cross JVM/JS): validated primitives in `net.wiringbits.common.models`. Pattern (Name.scala): `class Name private (val string: String) extends WrappedString`; `object Name extends WrappedString.Companion[Name] { override def validate(string): ValidationResult[Name]; override def trusted(string): Name }`. Uses `net.wiringbits.webapp.common.models.WrappedString` and `net.wiringbits.webapp.common.validators.ValidationResult` (`ValidationResult.Valid(input, value)` / `ValidationResult.Invalid(input = ..., error = ...)`). The Companion supplies the implicit `TextValidator[T]` and play-json Format; `FormField[T]` and `ValidatedTextInput[T: TextValidator]` rely on it. Specs: lib/common/shared/src/test/.../models/NameSpec.scala.
- lib/api/shared: Tapir endpoints (`api/endpoints/CategoriesEndpoints.scala`) and models (`api/models/categories/{CreateCategory,UpdateCategory,GetCategories,DeleteCategory}.scala`), each with play-json `Json.format` and a named `Schema.derived`. Current shapes: `CreateCategory.Request(name: String)`, `CreateCategory.Response(id: UUID, name: String)`, `UpdateCategory.Request(name: String)`, `UpdateCategory.Response()`, `GetCategories.Response(data: List[Response.Category])`, `Response.Category(id: UUID, name: String, createdAt: Instant)`. The package object `api/models/package.scala` has the Instant format and a schema for WrappedString. Option fields are nullable in Json.format (missing → None; None is omitted on write).
- server (Play): controllers → actions (`net.wiringbits.actions.categories.{Create,Update,Get,Delete}CategoryAction`) → validators (`net.wiringbits.validations`, plain objects that throw or fail Futures with RuntimeException(msg); see ValidatePasswordMatches) → repositories (`CategoriesRepository`) → DAOs (`repositories/daos/CategoryDAO.scala`, Anorm `SQL"""..."""` interpolation). Row parsers are in `repositories/daos/package.scala` (`categoryParser = Macro.parser[Category]("id","user_id","name","created_at","updated_at")`). Model: `repositories/models/Category.scala` (`Category(id, userId, name, createdAt, updatedAt)` and `Category.Create` with the same fields).
- Current category name rule lives inline in both Create/UpdateCategoryAction: `name.isBlank` → "The name is required"; `name.length > 25` → "Name must be 25 characters or less" (no trim; the value is stored raw). CategoriesControllerSpec asserts these exact messages; keep them.
- CategoriesRepository: `create(Category.Create)` (translates the unique violation `category_user_id_name_unique` → "A category with that name already exists"), `all(userId)`, `find(id, userId)`, `getOrCreate(userId, name)` (createIfAbsent ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id, else findByName CITEXT), `update(id, userId, name)` (DAO throws "Category not found" when 0 rows), `delete`. CreateCategoryAction uses getOrCreate, so a create with an existing name returns the existing row. getOrCreate callers: CreateCategoryAction, TelegramExpenseService (2x), UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction.
- GetCategoriesAction maps with Chimney `categories.map(_.transformInto[GetCategories.Response.Category])` (import io.scalaland.chimney.dsl.*). Chimney is a server dependency only, not on the web classpath.
- Evolutions: server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/N.sql, highest is 16.sql. Style: `-- !Ups`, SQL comment explaining the column, `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN x TEXT NULL;` (no Downs section in 16).
- AI: `server/.../services/StatementSuggestionsService.scala`. `private def categoryPrompt(categories, examples: List[(UUID,String)], row)` builds lines `- ${oneLine(c.name)}` plus `    example: ...` lines under the header "Categories, each with descriptions of transactions the user previously filed under it:". The answer instructions contain `<category name>`; the test fake classifies prompts by that string. `oneLine` is `private[services]` in the companion. `JevStatementSuggestionsService.predictCategory` builds `criteria: Map[categoryId.toString -> text]`, where text = `oneLine(name)` or `"${oneLine(name)}. Examples: a; b"`. Test fakes are inside the specs: StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec (recording Bedrock fake with `.prompts`, `categoryPrompts`; helper `category(name) = Category(UUID.randomUUID(), userId, name, now, now)`, positional) and JevStatementSuggestionsServiceSpec (recording JEV fake with `calls`, `categoryCalls.map(_.criteria)`; the same positional helper at line ~66). Both helpers must be updated when Category gains a field.
- MCP: `server/.../mcp/McpTools.scala` (tool metadata JSON; `ListCategories = "list_categories"` with a "description" text) and `McpDispatcher.scala` (`case McpTools.ListCategories => toolResult(id, getCategoriesAction(userId).map(Json.toJson(_)))`). Tests: server/src/test/scala/controllers/McpControllerSpec.scala ("return the authenticated user's categories via list_categories": parses `result.content[0].text` as JSON and then `data[*]`), and net/wiringbits/mcp/McpDispatcherSpec.scala (tool names list).
- Web (Scala.js + Slinky + MUI5): `web/.../components/pages/CategoriesPage.scala` contains `CategoriesPage` (AsyncComponent fetching getCategories) and `CategoryList`. CategoryList has a create form (useState newName → `createCategory(CreateCategory.Request(newName))`), inline rename per card (renamingId/renameValue → `updateCategory(id, UpdateCategory.Request(renameValue))`), search, pagination, and an error string state. Typed-form templates: `web/.../forms/UpdateInfoFormData.scala` (case class of `FormField[T]` extends `FormData[Req]`; `fields`, `formValidationErrors = List(fieldsError).flatten`, `submitRequest` via `field.valueOpt`; companion `initial(...)` building `new FormField(label=, name=, required=, `type`=, value = opt.map(x => ValidationResult.Valid(x.string, x)))`), `web/.../components/widgets/EditUserForm.scala` (StatefulFormData usage: `Hooks.useState(StatefulFormData(X.initial(...)))`, `setFormData(current => current.filling.copy(data = f(current.data)))`, `isSubmitButtonEnabled`, `_.submit`, `_.submitted`, `_.submissionFailed(msg)`, `isInputDisabled`, `isSubmitting`, `firstValidationError`, `ErrorLabel`), SignInForm.scala. Field updates use `field.updated(validationResult)`. Inputs: `web/.../ui/components/inputs/inputs.scala` (`object NameInput extends ValidatedTextInput[Name]`). `ValidatedTextInput.Props(field, disabled, onChange: ValidationResult[T] => Unit)` renders an MUI TextField with the error helperText. Form lib package: `net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.forms.{FormData, FormField, StatefulFormData}` (jar slinky-utils_sjs1_3 0.7.2 in ~/.cache/coursier; read it to confirm how optional untouched fields behave). Form specs: web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/*FormDataSpec.scala (pure AnyWordSpec + must Matchers).
- Category pickers use `MuiCompat.freeSoloAutocompleteProps(... getOptionLabel = AutocompleteLabels.categoryOptionLabel ...)`. Pure helpers are in `web/.../components/pages/AutocompleteLabels.scala`, tested by AutocompleteLabelsSpec. Main picker: `bankstatementreview/BankRowCreateExpenseForm.scala` (~line 409, `categoryIdOpt` state).
- Web call sites that construct category models (they must keep compiling): MerchantsPage.scala:158/162, CategoryResolver.scala:28/30 (named), BulkExpenseCreationPage.scala:160, BankRowCreateRefundForm.scala:116, plus many web specs that build `GetCategories.Response.Category(...)` positionally (BankStatementReviewLogicSpec, ReceiptsLogicSpec, BankRowCreate*FormSpec, BulkMerchantSetupPageSpec). Placing `description: Option[String] = None` LAST in Response.Category, after createdAt, avoids breaking positional call sites. Prefer that ordering.

CONVENTIONS / GOTCHAS
- Wartremover (Compile only, not tests): NamedArguments (2+ same-typed args must be passed by name; e.g. CategoryDAO.update(id = ..., userId = ..., name = ..., description = ..., updatedAt = ...)), StringPlusAny, PublicInference (give public vals/defs explicit types), Product/Serializable, Null, AsInstanceOf (banned in web pages; js.Dynamic only in compat/).
- Every category query must keep `WHERE user_id = ?`; list queries keep a stable `ORDER BY name`.
- Actions are flat for-comprehensions; conditionals go in `validations/` (RULE-BE-009). Errors are RuntimeException(message), which surface to the client as the message (tests use `.expectError` to compare the string).
- No silent defaults: never truncate or guess a description. Over-limit input fails with "Description must be 500 characters or less". Blank → None (NULL).
- Web: no object-level vals holding React elements; use `def` for elements reused in one render; use theme tokens / `var(--lc-*)` CSS vars, not hex. Copy the EditUserForm submit structure exactly (AP-FE-06). DOM tests need a RULE-TE-010 justification; prefer pure-function tests.
- Server tests: repository specs extend `RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils` (`withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }`, `createUser()`, `createCategory(userId, name = ...)`); controller specs use `withApiClient { implicit client => createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator).futureValue; ... }` (testcontainers Postgres). Test naming: method name as subject, no class-name prefix (RULE-TE-001).
- Verification: targeted `CI=true sbt "server/testOnly *XSpec"` / `"web/testOnly *XSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`; never the full `sbt test`. Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default shell node is v16). Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before committing.
- Repo is public: no PII in commits or the PR (no real bank or merchant names, amounts, filenames). No claude.ai links. Record spec deviations in the PR description's "Spec deviations" section: CategoryName primitive added; API keeps String/Option[String]; get-or-create leaves an existing description unchanged; JEV also gets descriptions.

findings.title: Category description and name inputs declare no max length in the API models

reason.text: Tapir maxLength validators would break the agreed behaviour. Requests would be rejected at decode time with Tapir's own error text instead of the required messages ('Name must be 25 characters or less', 'Description must be 500 characters or less'). A 500-character description with surrounding spaces is meant to be accepted and trimmed, but maxLength(500) on the raw string would reject it. The plan also says the API keeps String/Option[String] fields, so the limits stay in ValidateCategoryFields.
